{{nihongo|'''Ōasahiko Shrine'''|大麻比古神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Awa Province (Tokushima)]].

The precincts are designated as {{ill|Ōasayama Prefectural Natural Park|Q8081421|qid=Q8081421}}.

=== Enshrined God ===
; Main enshrined deity
* Cannabihikojin - The son of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tenhiwashi no Mikoto}}, and considered to be the ancestor of the Awaimbe clan.

; Deity enshrined
* {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|Q3090037|qid=Q3090037|lt=Sarutahiko Okami}} - It has been enshrined at {{ill|Mount Ōasa|Q11442028|qid=Q11442028|lt=Mt. Cannabis}} since ancient times, and is said to have been later enshrined there.From "Japanese Gods - Shrines and Sacred Places - 2 Sanyo and Shikoku" (hereinafter referred to as "Japanese Gods") <ref name="kamigami"> Kenichi Tanikawa (ed.) "Japanese Gods - Shrines and Sacred Places - 2 Sanyo and Shikoku" Hakusuisha Co., Ltd. October 1984. According to </ref>, in ancient times, the enshrined deity was Sarutahiko Okami, as stated in "{{ill|Dai Nippon Koku Ichinomiya Ki|ja|大日本国一宮記|qid=Q11435648}}", which was established in {{ill|Muromachi period|Q334845|qid=Q334845}}, and {{ill|Bunka|ca|Bunka|de|Bunka (Ära)|es|Bunka|fa|بونکا|fr|Ère Bunka|ia|Bunka|ja|文化 (元号)|ko|분카|ms|Zaman Bunka|ru|Бунка|simple|Bunka|sr|Бунка|sv|Bunka|tr|Bunka|zh|文化 (年號)|qid=Q1373146|lt=Bunka}} As can be seen in the ``Awa Koku Shikisha Ryakko'' written in 1815|Q6948}}, it is said that the {{ill|Urabe clan|fr|Clan Urabe|ja|卜部氏|ko|우라베씨|simple|Urabe clan|qid=Q11409028|lt=Urabe}} line of thought is generally unified in Sarutahiko Okami. In "Japanese Gods," on the other hand, on the side of shrines and priests, {{ill|Kyōhō|Q1145048|qid=Q1145048}}14 ({{ill|1729|Q6952|qid=Q6952}}) and {{jal ink|Horeki|Q1194397}} In the 4th year ({{ill|1754|ab|1754|af|1754|als|1754|am|1754 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1754|ar|1754|ary|1754|arz|1754|ast|1754|avk|1754|az|1754|azb|۱۷۵۴ (میلادی)|ba|1754 йыл|ban|1754|bar|1754|bcl|1754|be|1754|be_x_old|1754|bg|1754|bn|১৭৫৪|bo|༡༧༥༤ལོ།|bpy|মারি ১৭৫৪|br|1754|bs|1754.|ca|1754|cdo|1754 nièng|ceb|1754|ckb|١٧٥٤|co|1754|crh|1754|cs|1754|csb|1754|cv|1754|cy|1754|da|1754|de|1754|diq|1754|el|1754|eml|1754|eo|1754|es|1754|et|1754|eu|1754|fa|۱۷۵۴ (میلادی)|fi|1754|fo|1754|fr|1754|frp|1754|frr|1754|fur|1754|fy|1754|ga|1754|gan|1754年|gcr|1754|gd|1754|gl|1754|gv|1754|he|1754|hi|१७५४|hr|1754.|hsb|1754|ht|1754 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1754|hy|1754|hyw|1754 թուական|ia|1754|id|1754|ilo|1754|io|1754|is|1754|it|1754|ja|1754年|jv|1754|ka|1754|kaa|1754|kk|1754 жыл|kn|೧೭೫೪|ko|1754년|krc|1754 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1754|la|1754|lb|1754|lez|1754 йис|li|1754|lij|1754|lmo|1754|lt|1754 m.|lv|1754. gads|mai|१७५४|map_bms|1754|mdf|1754|mg|1754|mhr|1754|mi|1754|min|1754|mk|1754|mr|इ.स. १७५४|mrj|1754 и|ms|1754|my|၁၇၅၄|myv|1754 ие|mzn|۱۷۵۴|nah|1754|nap|1754|nds|1754|new|सन् १७५४|nl|1754|nn|1754|no|1754|nrm|1754|nso|1754|oc|1754|olo|1754|or|୧୭୫୪|os|1754-æм аз|pam|1754|pl|1754|pnb|1754|pt|1754|qu|1754|ro|1754|ru|1754 год|rue|1754|sa|१७५४|sah|1754|scn|1754|sd|1754ع|se|1754|sh|1754.|shn|1754|simple|1754|sk|1754|sl|1754|smn|1754|sq|1754|sr|1754|su|1754|sv|1754|sw|1754|szl|1754|ta|1754|te|1754|tg|Соли 1754|th|พ.ศ. 2297|tk|1754|tl|1754|tly|1754|tr|1754|tt|1754 ел|ug|1754 - يىلى|uk|1754|ur|1754ء|uz|1754|vec|1754|vi|1754|vls|1754|vo|1754|wa|1754|war|1754|wuu|1754年|xmf|1754|yi|1754|zh|1754年|zh_min_nan|1754 nî|zh_yue|1754年|qid=Q7623}}), the district magistrate said, ``The ritual of worshiping Sarutahiko Omikami, which is the object of worship. As I have written above, Sarutahiko Okami was originally enshrined at the top of Mt. Marijuana, and the original main deity was {{ill|Otori-sama|Q10939697|qid=Q10939697|lt=Amenohi Washi no Mikoto}} He states that he seems to have continued his efforts to attach himself to the ancestor god of the {{ill|Inbe clan|fa|خاندان اینبه|ja|忌部氏|pl|Inbe (ród)|simple|Inbe clan|th|ตระกูลอิมเบะ|zh|忌部氏|qid=Q8189229|lt=Awa Inbe clan}}, implicitly denying Sarutahiko no Okami.In the Jindai volume of "{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}", the distant ancestor of the Awaimbe clan is Tenhiwashi no Mikoto, and in "{{ill|Kogo Shūi|de|Kogo Shūi|es|Kogo Shūi|fr|Kogo shūi|id|Kogo Shūi|it|Kogo shūi|ja|古語拾遺|ko|고어습유|th|โคโงะชูอิ|uk|Кого Шюї|zh|古語拾遺|qid=Q531555}}" {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amantomi no Mikoto}} (Amenotomi no Mikoto) led the grandchildren of Tenhiwashi no Mikoto and sent them to Awa Province in search of fertile land, and brought seeds of {{ill|Paper mulberry|an|Broussonetia papyrifera|ar|توت الورق|arz|بروسونته ورقيه|az|Kağız kağızağacı|azb|کاغیزی آغاج|be|Broussonetia papyrifera|ca|Morera de paper|ceb|Broussonetia papyrifera|cs|Papírovník čínský|de|Papiermaulbeerbaum|el|Βρουσονέτια η παπυροφόρος|es|Broussonetia papyrifera|eu|Paper-masustondo|fa|توت کاغذی|fi|Paperimulperio|fr|Broussonetia papyrifera|he|תות נייר|hu|Kínai papíreperfa|hy|Բրուսոնեթիա թղթյա|id|Daluang|it|Broussonetia papyrifera|ja|カジノキ|ko|꾸지나무|la|Broussonetia papyrifera|lfn|Morero turces|mad|Dhâlubâng|mi|Aute|mk|Broussonetia papyrifera|ml|പേപ്പർ മൾബെറി|ms|Jeluang|my|သာလဲပင်|nl|Papiermoerbei|no|Papirmorbærtre|pl|Brusonecja chińska|pt|Amoreira-do-papel|pwn|quljicaca|ru|Бруссонетия бумажная|simple|Paper mulberry|sr|Дудовац|su|Daluang|sv|Pappersmullbärsträd|th|ปอสา|tl|Papel moras|to|Hiapo|tr|Broussonetia papyrifera|uk|Broussonetia papyrifera|vi|Dướng|war|Broussonetia papyrifera|zh|構樹|zh_min_nan|Lo̍k-á-chhiū|zh_yue|構樹|qid=Q389185|lt=grain}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=hemp}}. However, according to "Japanese Gods," Noguchi Elder of Awa Province was the {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ceb|Awa (baranggay)|ckb|پارێزگای ئاوا (چیبا)|cs|Provincie Awa (Čiba)|de|Provinz Awa (Chiba)|es|Provincia de Awa (Chiba)|fa|ولایت آوا (چیبا)|fr|Province d'Awa (Chiba)|gl|Provincia de Awa, Chiba|hak|Awa-koet (Tōkaidō)|id|Provinsi Awa (Chiba)|it|Awa (provincia, Chiba)|ja|安房国|ko|아와국 (도카이도)|lt|Avos žemė (Čiba)|nl|Awa (provincie in Chiba)|pt|Província de Awa (Chiba)|ru|Ава (Канто)|simple|Awa Province (Chiba)|sk|Awa (provincia, Čiba)|sr|Провинција Ава (Хоншу)|tr|Awa (vilayet, Chiba)|uk|Провінція Ава (Канто)|zh|安房國|zh_min_nan|Awa-kok (Tôkaidô)|zh_yue|安房國|qid=Q1053044}}{{jalink|Shimodate Matsubara Shrine|Q1136 According to the Inabe clan genealogy handed down in 1262, he proposed the theory that Marihiko-no-Mikoto was the son of Tenhiwashi-no-Mikoto, also known as Tsukuimino-no-Mikoto, and that his daughter was Chikaehime-no-Mikoto.

{{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}} Previously, the enshrined deity was Sarutahiko Okami and the Awa-Ibe clan's ancestor Tenhi-Washi no Mikoto, but after the Meiji period it was Sarutahiko Okami and Tenta-tama-no-Mikoto based on ancient legends, but according to "Japanese Gods," Sadazane Yamaguchi further developed the idea of the Inabe clan's ancestral deity and advocated it. ``As Tenhiwashi no Mikoto is the ancestor of Awa Ibe, ({{ill|Inbe Shrine|ja|忌部神社|simple|Inbe Shrine|qid=Q11490722}} is called Asue no Mikoto due to the shrine or place name of Inabe, (our company) enshrines the great ancestor Tentatama no Mikoto and calls it Cannabihikojin,'' the theory that forms the basis of current cannabis beliefs.In the same book, in the myth, Tentadama no Mikoto, the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amatsukami}}, who accompanied {{ill|Tenson kōrin|Q1084733|qid=Q1084733}} as one of the five attendants, and the {{ill|Kateri Tekakwitha|Q609|qid=Q609|ltq=Q609}}'s Sarutahiko no Okami originally belonged to a different lineage of gods, and while he states that it is not necessarily clear why these two deities, which are essentially in conflict with one another, are enshrined in the same shrine, he speculates about the circumstances under which Sarutahiko no Okami was enshrined as follows.

According to the Inabe clan genealogy at Shimotatematsubara Shrine, the other name of Maribhiko-no-Mikoto is Tsukumi-no-Mikoto, and his daughter is called Senkaehime-no-Mikoto, but these divinities are ``Tsukuimi'' and ``Chikae,'' both deities with names related to ports. In our case, it is thought that as the power of the Ibe clan declined, the character of Tsumikomi no Mikoto was forgotten, and that his function as a god of ports and a god of transportation, which became increasingly important with economic development, remained. It is said that after the fall of the Ibe clan, the divinity of Sarutahiko Okami, the god of the streets and the god of traffic, was probably attached to it due to {{ill|Kōshin|Q3082157|qid=Q3082157}}, which became popular among folk during the Muromachi period.

=== History ===
According to the shrine's legend, during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|qid=Q200188}}, Tentomi no Mikoto, the grandson of Tentai Tama no Mikoto, led the ancestors of the Awa Inbe clan and moved to Awa Province, where he cultivated hemp and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=kozo}} seeds. The company is said to have its origins in the enshrining of the ancestral deity, Tenta Tama-no-Mikoto (Kannabihiko-kami), as the guardian deity of Awa Province.

"{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}" {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} According to the article dated January 27, 1997 ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), our company has been conferred the rank of {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} from {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Fifth Rank Lower}} to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Fifth Rank Upper}}. According to an article in "Nihon Sandai Jiroku", our company further states that in the article dated April 23, 9th year of Jogan ({{ill|867|Q30347|qid=Q30347}}), ink|878|Q23910}}) In the article of April 14th, he advanced to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower}}, and in the article of November 1st, Genkei 7 ({{ill|883|Q30355|qid=Q30355}}), he advanced to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Upper}}. In {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Extension}}5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), it was promoted to Shikinai-sha and Meishin-taisha Shrine according to the ``{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}''.From the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}} to the {{ill|Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205}}, {{ill|Jingū-ji|Q1074971|qid=Q1074971}}, which essentially operated shrines based on the {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|Q2279088|qid=Q2279088}} philosophy, were established in various places, but ``Shokoku Ichi no Miya'' <ref name="shokoku">Koichiro Irie "Shokoku Ichi no Miya" Mobile Classroom Publishing Department June 2001. </ref> states that the first temple {{ill|Ryōzen-ji (Naruto)|Q1085463|qid=Q1085463|lt=Ryozenji}} of {{ill|Shikoku Pilgrimage|Q1972399|qid=Q1972399}} was our Jingu temple. However, from "Basic Research on the Ichinomiya System in Medieval Countries" <ref name="kiso"> edited by the Ichinomiya System in Medieval Countries Research Group, "Basic Research on the Ichinomiya System in Medieval Countries", Iwata Shoin Co., Ltd., February 2000. </ref> states that {{ill|Bettō-ji|Q11396755|qid=Q11396755}} is unknown.

『{{ill|Chōya Gunsai|Q11517735|qid=Q11517735}} In Volume 6, there is a message that the god of cannabis in Awa Province was cursed due to excessive impurity in the rituals, so a messenger should be sent to perform a mid-purification and purify the people. There is a {{ill|Department of Divinities|Q2264720|qid=Q2264720}} sojo dated June 10, 743}}4 ({{ill|1080|Q19448|qid=Q19448}}).Although our company is listed as Ichinomiya in Awa Province in the ``Dainihonkoku Ichinomiya'', which is said to have been established during the Muromachi period, in ``Basic Research on the Ichinomiya System in Medieval Countries'' <ref name="kiso" />, (Japan)|Q264012|During the Nanbokucho era}}, our company boasted a traditional shrine status and was close to the guardian post of the {{ill|Hosokawa clan|Q2736120|qid=Q2736120|lt=Hosokawa clan}}. (Tokushima City)|Q11352598|Ichinomiya Shrine}} It is considered that it has been given the status of a new Ichinomiya shrine in Awa Province.

"Visiting the No. 1 Shrines in the Nation" <ref name="zenkoku"> Edited by the No. 1 Shrines in the Nation Official guidebook "Visiting the No. 1 Shrines in the Nation" by the No. 1 Shrines in the Nation From December 2008. According to </ref>, it was protected by the Hosokawa clan and the {{ill|Miyoshi clan|Q2975329|qid=Q2975329}} during the Muromachi period, and by the {{ill|Tokushima Domain|Q3034557|qid=Q3034557}} lord {{ill|Hachisuka clan|Q2975261|qid=Q2975261|lt=Hachisuka family}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}}. In addition, in the 4th year of Kyoho ({{ill|1719|Q6902|qid=Q6902}}), the highest divine rank of {{ill|Senior First Rank|Q11123258|qid=Q11123258}} was conferred.

In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}), it was promoted to Kokuheichusha, and in Meiji 13 ({{ill|1880|Q7806|qid=Q7806}}), the main hall and the rest were built using national funds.In {{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}}8 ({{ill|1919|Q2157|qid=Q2157}}), a stone arch bridge was completed behind the main shrine. This bridge is called {{ill|German Bridge|Q11322494|qid=Q11322494}} because it was built based on the proposal and construction of German soldiers who had been imprisoned in {{ill|Bandō prisoner-of-war camp|Q324270|qid=Q324270}} as prisoners of war during {{ill|World War I|Q361|qid=Q361}} when they returned home.

After the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Old Shrine Ranking}} was abolished after {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=World War II}}, it became {{ill|Beppyo shrine|Q10898274|qid=Q10898274}}, which was encompassed by {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|Q908077|qid=Q908077}}. === Precincts ===
[[File:Oasahiko-jinja, honden-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|main hall}}]]
[[File:Oasahiko-jinja, kusu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Oasahiko-jinja (Naruto City designated natural monument)}}]]
* Main shrine - Rebuilt with national funds in 1880.
* Inner worship hall and outer worship hall - Rebuilt in 1970.
* Noritoden - Rebuilt in 1970.
* Kojin Sapporo
* Jinko
* Shinbasha
* Shrine office
* Awarding place
* Okumiya Aihaisho
* Sanshuden
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=large camphor}} - A sacred tree said to be over 1000 years old. Designated by Naruto City {{ill|Natural monument|Q23790|qid=Q23790}}.
* German Bridge - See "{{ill|German Bridge|Q11322494|qid=Q11322494}}".
* Megane Bridge - Built by German soldiers who were imprisoned in {{ill|Bandō prisoner-of-war camp|Q324270|qid=Q324270}} during the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Taisho period}}.
* Otorii - You can see it when you pass by {{ill|Ryōzen-ji (Naruto)|Q1085463|qid=Q1085463|lt=Reizanji}} and go under the elevated {{ill|Takamatsu Expressway|Q7677132|qid=Q7677132}}. From here, a path lined with pine trees continues for about 800 meters. Rebuilt with steel pipes in 2002. Height: 14.6m.
* Okumiyamine Shrine - Enshrined at the top of Mt. Oasayama at an altitude of 538m. Climbing for about an hour and a half.
